o: The part of the hoistway below the lowest landing, which needs waterproofing and drainage

questions.n: The pit holds the buffers and the lower end of the rails. It is below grade in many buildings, so it must be kept dry.

questions.q: Why must the hoistway, pit and overhead sizes come from the chosen maker's data?
o: The code fixes one size for every elevator
They change with capacity, speed, drive type and maker
Only the door width matters to the structure
The fire code alone sets them
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: A generic diagram shows the parts but not the numbers. Real shafts are laid out from the selected model's drawings.

questions.q: Why is a hospital bed elevator car deeper than it is wide?
o: To reduce the hoistway width for the structure
Because deeper cars travel faster
To fit a bed or stretcher lengthwise with attendants
To make room for a second door
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: A hospital bed is about 2.2 m long, so bed cars are about 2.5 to 2.7 m deep.

questions.q: Why are access paths to elevator machinery important?
o: So the machine can be run from the lobby
So the car can be parked outside the hoistway
To give the hoistway natural ventilation
Technicians must reach the equipment safely to service and replace it
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Drives, controllers and ropes need regular service. Machine spaces need safe stairs, doors and lighting.

questions.q: Why must an elevator hoistway stack straight up through the floors?
o: The car needs a continuous, straight travel path
Stacking removes the need for guide rails
Stacking gives the shaft natural ventilation
Offsets are fine as long as the car can tilt
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Rails run straight from pit to overhead. A shaft that shifts between floors cannot hold a conventional elevator.

questions.q: Under the BP 344 IRR, what minimum clear space must an elevator lobby have?
questions.ref: BP 344 Revised IRR (2024), Appendix A, Sec. 8.11
questions.n: The 1,800 mm square lets a wheelchair user turn around in front of the elevator.

questions.q: Which item needs early coordination because it affects structure and floor plans the most?
o: Car interior finishes
Hall lantern style
Hoistway location and size
Call-button style
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Hoistways run through every floor and need pits and overheads. Finishes can be chosen late.

questions.n: If the car overruns the top floor, the overhead keeps it clear of the ceiling. Its height depends on speed and model.

questions.q: Why is a service elevator often kept apart from the main passenger lobby?
o: To keep deliveries, carts and waste out of public circulation
Service elevators cannot stop at lobby floors
Codes ban shared lobbies in every building
Passenger elevators cannot carry any goods
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: Hotels, hospitals and offices route housekeeping, refuse and deliveries through back-of-house cores.

questions.q: Why should the elevator lobby be visible and easy to reach from the main entrance?
o: It lowers the fire rating needed for the shaft
It helps people find their way and avoids cross-traffic
It makes the car lighter
It removes the need for signs
questions.ref: ASME A17.1 elevator and escalator terminology; Strakosch, The Vertical Transportation Handbook
questions.n: BP 344 also puts accessible elevators within 30 m of the entrance.
